caption: What if you had a newborn's body again? You'd have around 300 bones. Many fuse as you grow, leaving an adult with 206. Your kneecaps would be soft cartilage, not bone, and only start hardening in the toddler years. Your skull bones wouldn't be joined yet, leaving soft spots that close later. You'd see clearly only about 20 to 30 cm away, roughly the distance to Mumma's face while feeding. In an 1891 study of 60 newborns, every baby held onto a rod for at least 10 seconds, and one hung on for 2 minutes 35 seconds (never try this on a real baby!). Your heart would race at about 120 to 160 beats a minute. Your brain would be only a quarter of adult size, and it doubles in the first year. Plot twist: you'd cry loudly but with no tears. Tear ducts aren't fully working yet, so real tears usually show up at around 3 to 4 weeks. Happy Children's Day week! Which baby fact shocked YOU? 👇
